architect.rationale:
SHAPE: single-loop. App 1 IS a git repo (on `main`), so fan-out is mechanically possible - but it is not warranted.
The only plausible diamond split is s1=build-time transformer, s2=popover.inline.ts+scss, s3=Playwright spec. Those file sets are disjoint, but the slices are NOT independent: s2 consumes the exact data-* attribute contract s1 emits (producer/consumer), and s3's done_when (npx playwright test popover.spec.ts) requires a full `npx quartz build` with s1 registered AND s2's runtime behavior present - it cannot be checked without the other two. That fails the diamond's "done_when checkable in isolation" test. Total diff is ~1 new file plus ~80 changed lines across 2 existing files: one reviewable diff.

DO-NOT-MODIFY JUDGMENT (stated explicitly for the human reviewer, per the task): I do NOT need to resolve the ambiguity, because I chose a mechanism sanctioned under BOTH readings of the rule.
App 1/CLAUDE.md:34 says quartz/plugins/ is "stable and should not be changed". But the SAME file, at lines 107-112 ("Adding a New Transformer Plugin"), gives explicit step-by-step instructions to (1) create a file in quartz/plugins/transformers/, (2) export it from quartz/plugins/transformers/index.ts, (3) add it to quartz.config.ts, (4) add tests in quartz/plugins/transformers/tests/. That is direct internal evidence the line-34 rule targets pre-existing upstream Quartz core files, not the addition of new bespoke transformers.
Therefore: ADD a new transformer file; do NOT modify linkfavicons.ts. This keeps the working favicon path untouched, produces a cleaner diff, and violates no reading of the Do-Not-Modify table. The only edit to an existing file under quartz/plugins/ is a single one-line export in index.ts, which CLAUDE.md line 110 explicitly instructs. quartz.config.ts, quartz/components/ and quartz/styles/ are all listed as editable.
I did NOT choose the post-build Python script alternative under scripts/: it would have to re-parse and rewrite already-emitted HTML in public/, duplicating link-walking logic the rehype tree gives for free, and it would run outside `npx quartz build` (deploy.yaml line 33) so Cloudflare Pages would ship un-enriched HTML unless CI were also changed - and .github/workflows/ is hard off-limits.

MECHANISM, and the honest statement of what actually fixes the bug:
The fix is the BUILD-TIME frame-policy gate, not the runtime timeout. A cross-origin iframe blocked by X-Frame-Options/CSP still fires `load`, and its contentDocument/contentWindow.location are unreadable cross-origin - so there is NO client-side signal that distinguishes "blocked" from "loaded". A builder must not waste time trying contentDocument sniffing; it cannot work. The timeout (item 3 of the task) is genuinely useful, but only for slow/hung frames, not for detecting blocking.
So the invariant that makes "never show a raw browser refused-to-connect message" actually hold is: DEFAULT IS THE CARD. An iframe is attempted only when a build-time probe affirmatively proved that origin permits framing. Missing, stale or uncrawled data means card. Fail-safe, not fail-open.

COST (measured, not guessed): content/ contains 641 unique external URLs across 246 unique origins. One GET per URL yields BOTH the frame headers and the HTML for title/description - one fetch, both outcomes. The existing favicon cache is gitignored (.gitignore:31), so it re-fetches on every CI build; for 641 full page fetches that is too slow to repeat. Hence the recommendation to COMMIT the new preview cache so CI builds are warm and only newly-added links are fetched. No .gitignore edit is needed (the existing ignore pattern is specific to .faviconUrls.txt).

AMBIGUITY IN THE GOAL - two readings, I recommend the first:
(A) "Transclusion" means the user wants to see remote content, so keep the iframe where it legitimately works, and make everything else a good card. RECOMMENDED - it is fix-and-improve, preserves the existing feature's intent, and the task explicitly says not to rewrite the popover system.
(B) Kill the iframe entirely; always card. Simpler, faster, better privacy (no third-party request on hover), and removes a class of bug permanently - but it deletes a feature the run name says the user wanted. If the human prefers (B) at the gate, this plan degrades cleanly: drop the frameability probe and the runtime timeout, keep the metadata fetch and the card. Say so at the gate and the builder scope shrinks.

plan.intent:
Make external-link popovers never surface a browser frame-block error, by gating iframes behind a build-time frameability probe and defaulting to a rich metadata card. Ordered steps:

1. NEW quartz/plugins/transformers/linkpreviews.ts, exporting AddLinkPreviews(), modeled structurally on linkfavicons.ts (same logger_utils logger, same cache-read-at-module-load / write-cache-after-visit shape, same never-fail-the-build try/catch-and-continue posture).
   - For each a[href] with an http(s) href whose hostname is not App 1: one GET (not HEAD - many origins 405 HEAD, and CSP frame-ancestors usually only ships on the document response), with AbortSignal.timeout(REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS) and a bounded concurrency pool (MAX_CONCURRENT_FETCHES).
   - From that single response derive BOTH: (a) frameability, from the x-frame-options header and the frame-ancestors directive of content-security-policy; (b) metadata, by parsing the body with cheerio (already a dependency, package.json:154/175, currently used only in quartz/cli/handlers.ts) for og:title falling back to <title>, and og:description falling back to meta[name=description].
   - frameable is true ONLY IF: no XFO header (or an XFO value that is neither DENY nor SAMEORIGIN) AND (no frame-ancestors directive OR frame-ancestors permits App 1, e.g. contains *). frame-ancestors 'none' and 'self' are NOT frameable. Anything unparseable, errored, timed out, or non-2xx is not frameable. Default deny.
   - Truncate description at MAX_DESCRIPTION_CHARS. All limits and timeouts are SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE named constants (CLAUDE.md: no magic numbers).
   - Bake onto the anchor via hast properties (rehype escapes attribute values, so no injection at emit time): data-preview-title, data-preview-description, and data-preview-frameable="true" emitted ONLY when true - absence must mean "do not frame".
   - Cache to quartz/plugins/transformers/.linkPreviews.json keyed by full URL: { title, description, frameable, fetchedAt }. Cache negative and failed results too (linkfavicons.ts:226 precedent) so a dead host is not re-fetched every build. COMMIT this file to git, unlike .faviconUrls.txt, so CI builds are warm - 641 cold fetches per deploy is not acceptable.
   - Honor an env escape hatch (SKIP_LINK_PREVIEWS) that uses cache-only and performs zero network I/O, so npx quartz build --serve local iteration stays fast.
   - Explicit TypeScript types throughout, no any, strict-null-safe (CLAUDE.md Code Standards).

2. Register it: one export line in quartz/plugins/transformers/index.ts, and one Plugin.AddLinkPreviews() line in quartz.config.ts placed immediately after Plugin.AddFavicons() (both walk anchors; keeping them adjacent and after CrawlLinks means hrefs are already normalized).

3. quartz/components/scripts/popover.inline.ts - rewire ONLY the external branch. Do not touch createPopover's internal-link path, setPopoverPosition, or animate().
   - Read data-preview-* off the anchor. If data-preview-frameable is not "true" (including absent, i.e. the uncrawled or stale case), build the card directly and NEVER create an iframe. This is the actual fix for lines 41-82.
   - Upgrade buildExternalLinkSummary into a rich card: title (from data-preview-title, falling back to link text, falling back to hostname), description, hostname, and the favicon already emitted next to the link by AddFavicons (reuse the existing img.favicon src from the DOM rather than re-deriving a path - no coupling from runtime code to linkfavicons internals).
   - SECURITY, non-negotiable: the card currently uses innerHTML with interpolated values (popover.inline.ts:19-23 and 52-55). Title and description are now REMOTE-CONTROLLED strings, so innerHTML becomes a real injection vector. Build the card with createElement plus textContent only. Remove innerHTML from both helpers.
   - For the frameable path only, keep the existing iframe, sandbox and no-referrer setup and add a real timeout: if no load event within EXTERNAL_PREVIEW_TIMEOUT_MS, replace the frame with the card, add external-preview-frame--fallback, and dispatch EXTERNAL_PREVIEW_LOADED_EVENT so the existing reposition handler at lines 141-147 still fires. Clear the timer in the load and error handlers and in the returned cleanup, so a fast mouseout cannot leak a timer or mutate a detached popover.

4. quartz/components/styles/popover.scss - extend the existing .external-link-preview and .external-preview-frame--fallback rules (lines 139-166) to style the richer card (favicon plus title row, description). Additive only; no changes to positioning or animation rules.

5. Tests.
   - NEW quartz/plugins/transformers/tests/linkpreviews.test.ts (Jest): frameability parsing table - XFO DENY / SAMEORIGIN / absent / garbage; CSP frame-ancestors 'none' / 'self' / * / absent; both headers present and disagreeing. Metadata extraction: og:* preferred over <title> and meta description, missing tags, truncation at MAX_DESCRIPTION_CHARS. Cache round-trip including negative caching. A fetch rejection or timeout must not throw out of the plugin. Mock fetch; NO real network in unit tests.
   - quartz/components/scripts/tests/popover.test.ts (Jest): an anchor without data-preview-frameable produces a card and creates NO iframe element; an anchor with data-preview-frameable="true" creates an iframe; the timeout elapsing swaps frame for card and dispatches the loaded event; a title containing markup renders as literal text (regression test for the innerHTML fix).
   - quartz/components/tests/popover.spec.ts (Playwright): the existing test "External links render sandboxed previews on hover" (lines 49-62) asserts the CURRENT BROKEN BEHAVIOR - it hovers .external (github.com, which sends X-Frame-Options: DENY) and asserts an iframe appears. Rewrite it to assert a card and the ABSENCE of an iframe for a non-frameable link. Keep the fallback test (lines 65-86) but retarget it at the timeout path.

architect.edges: single slice - no edges. Internally sequential: transformer plus config (steps 1-2) must land before popover.inline.ts (step 3) consumes the data-preview-* contract, and the Playwright spec (step 5) requires a full build with both present. This forced ordering is precisely why this is a sequence, not a diamond.
not_doing: NOT modifying quartz/plugins/transformers/linkfavicons.ts. The new transformer is additive and reads no linkfavicons internals; the runtime card reuses the already-rendered img.favicon element in the DOM instead.
NOT restructuring createPopover's internal-link path, fetchWithMetaRedirect, popover_helpers.ts, setPopoverPosition, or component_script_utils.ts animate(). Not broken; out of scope.
NOT touching positioning or animation CSS in popover.scss - additive card styling only.
NOT building a server-side iframe proxy or CORS relay. Deployment is static Cloudflare Pages (deploy.yaml:96); there is no request-time server to host one.
NOT attempting client-side detection of a blocked iframe via contentDocument or contentWindow. Cross-origin, impossible by design. Do not let a builder try.
NOT modifying .github/workflows/, package-lock.json, or patches/ (CLAUDE.md Do Not Modify).
NOT adding new npm dependencies. cheerio is already a dependency.
NOT fetching og:image or building image or screenshot thumbnails. Scope creep; the card is title + description + domain + existing favicon.
NOT adding a hand-maintained domain allowlist or denylist. The frameability probe derives the list at build time; a hand-maintained list would rot.

findings.issue: The committed cache's frameable booleans were all computed by the OLD (buggy) parser during attempt 1's build and are served from cache, so commit f74b13e's parser fix does not recompute them until CACHE_TTL_MS elapses. I closed this gap by hand: live re-probed all 94 frameable origins through the new isFrameable and found no consistent false positive. The shipped output is correct today, but it is correct because I checked, not because the build recomputed it. A one-off cold rebuild (or deleting the cache once) before merge would make the committed booleans provably products of the fixed parser.

Build-time probe fidelity: node's fetch has no browser UA and no cookies, so anti-bot origins can serve it a different response than a real visitor gets. Two entries cached metadata from an interstitial: opg.optica.org has title "Radware Captcha Page" and anandtech.com has "Checking your browser", both with frameable:true. Concrete user-visible result: the popover card and header for those two links show "Radware Captcha Page" / "Checking your browser" instead of the article title. 2 of 560 entries (0.36%). Cosmetic, does not produce a block page, and interstitial detection is new scope attempt 1 was not rejected for; flagged so the human knows the limitation exists, not as a request to fix it now.

The CACHE_TTL_MS doc comment justifies the TTL by saying a re-probe is "spread across the cache's natural age spread". That is not true of the current cache: all 560 entries carry fetchedAt within the same two minutes (2026-08-26T05:03-05:04), so they all expire on the same day and one build around 2026-09-25 will re-probe all 560 URLs at once. That build still succeeds (MAX_CONCURRENT_FETCHES bounds concurrency, REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS bounds each request), it is just slow, roughly once a month. Only the comment's justification is wrong, not the code.

When an expired entry is re-probed and the network is down or the host is transiently failing, createFailedPreview() overwrites a previously good entry with frameable:false and an empty title/description, and that degradation is then committed. The direction is fail-safe (card, never a block page) and it matches the linkfavicons.ts negative-caching precedent, so not a defect, but a CI build on a bad network day can quietly strip titles from the committed cache.

The guard "if (!popoverElement) throw new Error(...)" is unreachable: popoverElement is typed HTMLElement and every branch above either assigns it or throws into the catch. Harmless dead guard, carried over from attempt 1 and unchanged in f74b13e.

Carried forward unchanged from the attempt-1 review and still true: writeCacheToFile() runs once per parsed page inside the workerpool, so worker threads race and last-write-wins can drop entries. Both failure modes are fail-safe (a missing entry means card; torn JSON means an empty map). linkfavicons.ts has the identical pattern, so it is precedent-consistent, not new.

previous_attempts.summary: The shape of the fix is right and I verified it end to end: `npm run check` exit 0, `npm test` 29 suites / 1474 tests exit 0, grep innerHTML on popover.inline.ts returns 0 matches, the four Desktop Chrome External|Frameable Playwright tests pass first try, and the emitted HTML escapes remote-derived attribute values (an arxiv title containing quotes emits "). The commit touches neither .claude/settings.json nor content/changelog.md. Scope discipline holds: linkfavicons.ts, popover_helpers.ts, the internal createPopover path and all positioning/animation code are untouched, and the scss change is 7 added lines. The timeout is genuinely safe: load and error both clearTimeout, the callback bails on !popoverElement.isConnected, and per the HTML spec clearTimeout still cancels an already-expired-but-unrun timer, so no card can replace a good iframe and the worst case is a closure held for 5s. I reject on one thing, and it is the one thing this run exists to prevent. parseFrameAncestors splits the CSP header on ";" only. A CSP header value may carry multiple policies separated by ",", and Headers.get() joins duplicate Content-Security-Policy response headers with ", " - so the first directive of every policy after the first is swallowed into the previous directive's token list and never inspected. Given "default-src 'self', frame-ancestors 'none'" the function returns null and isFrameable returns true, the anchor gets data-preview-frameable="true", the popover builds an iframe, and the browser paints its refused-to-connect page. That is the exact bug this run exists to fix. This is not a hypothetical header shape: docs.google.com serves a comma-joined multi-policy CSP today (verified live), and an origin plus a CDN/WAF each emitting their own CSP header is routine. I probed all 94 hosts the committed cache currently marks frameable against a spec-correct parser and found zero present-day false positives, so shipped output is correct right now by luck rather than by construction - and since entries are cached forever with no TTL, one false positive would be frozen into a committed file permanently. The fix is about three lines plus one test row.

findings.issue: parseFrameAncestors splits only on ";", so it misses frame-ancestors when that directive is the first directive of any policy after the first in a multi-policy CSP value. Concrete: new Headers({"content-security-policy": "default-src 'self', frame-ancestors 'none'"}) -> parseFrameAncestors returns null -> isFrameable returns true -> applyPreviewToNode stamps data-preview-frameable="true" -> popover.inline.ts:207 builds an iframe for an origin that denies framing -> browser refused-to-connect page inside the popover. Identical failure whenever an origin and a CDN/WAF each send a Content-Security-Policy header, because Headers.get() joins duplicates with ", ". docs.google.com serves a comma-joined multi-policy CSP today (verified live), so the header shape is real, not contrived. FIX: split the header value on "," into policies first, then split each policy on ";", and treat frame-ancestors found in ANY policy as restricting unless its source list contains "*" (browsers enforce the intersection of all delivered policies). Add an isFrameable table row for the comma case; the table at linkpreviews.test.ts:65-91 has no coverage for it, which is why this shipped green.

The committed cache never expires. fetchedAt is written but never read, so once a URL is cached it is never re-probed on any later build. A site that adds X-Frame-Options after being cached frameable:true keeps getting an iframe forever, silently, until a human hand-edits the JSON. Combined with the blocker above, a single mis-parse becomes permanent. Either honour fetchedAt with a max age, or document the manual invalidation procedure where a maintainer will find it.

writeCacheToFile() runs once per parsed page, and quartz/processors/parse.ts:175 runs htmlPlugins inside a workerpool with maxWorkers=concurrency. Each worker thread holds its own module-level previewCache loaded at import, so workers race on the same file and last-write-wins can drop entries another worker discovered. Not a correctness hazard (a missing entry means card; a torn file fails JSON.parse and degrades to an empty map, both fail-safe) but the committed cache may be silently incomplete and CI will re-fetch those URLs. linkfavicons.ts:539 has the identical pattern, so this is precedent-consistent, not new.

targetUrl.search is stripped before the iframe src is set, but normalizePreviewUrl (linkpreviews.ts:212) keeps the query string in the cache key. A query-bearing link is therefore probed as .../edit?gid=0 and then framed as .../edit. Pre-existing on main (the old line 62 used the same stripped URL), not introduced here, but the build-time proof and the runtime request are now nominally about two different URLs.

The rewritten "Frameable external links render a sandboxed iframe preview" test dropped the previous await expect(previewFrame).toBeVisible() and now asserts only the sandbox attribute. toHaveAttribute still requires the element to resolve so it is not vacuous, but it is a small weakening of an existing assertion with no stated reason.

An empty X-Frame-Options value ("") falls through to the CSP check and can end up frameable:true. Browsers do ignore an empty/invalid XFO value so this is defensible, but it is the one place the "any value really, be conservative" instruction recorded in builders.s1 notes(1) is not applied.
